name: Grand Hyatt Bali
positioning: Family-friendly beachfront resort in Nusa Dua, Bali, with rooms, suites and villas set across four villages in contemporary Balinese style
best_for: Families who want a kids club and a pool with waterslides
Travelers who want a beachfront base in Nusa Dua with several pools and a spa

facts.text: Grand Hyatt Bali is a family-friendly beachfront resort in Nusa Dua, Bali.
Rooms, suites and villas are set across four villages, all designed in contemporary Balinese style.
Guest rooms have teakwood and marble floors from Central Java, a marble bath with a separate shower and a private balcony.
Ocean-view rooms have a private balcony overlooking the Indian Ocean's white sandy beaches.
The villas include a private pool.
The resort has five swimming pools.
At the Oceania Kids Club, children learn about Balinese culture and explore the resort's local flora and fauna.
The Bay Club Fitness Center has cardio equipment, machine weights, squash courts and a yoga studio.
The rooftop Salsa Bar has panoramic views of the Nusa Dua coastline.
Wedding venues range from tropical gardens to a white, sandy beachfront.
The resort is steps from the Bali Collection shopping center.
The hotel is 15 minutes from Ngurah Rai International Airport.

highlights.text: The secluded Balinese Feature Pool has emerald green water and cascading waterfalls.
The lagoon-style Main Pool is surrounded by tropical gardens, and the River Pool has two waterslides.
Kriya Spa draws inspiration from Balinese water palaces and offers bespoke spa and wellness treatments by trained therapists.
At Pasar Senggol, guests dine in an open-air amphitheatre while watching live Balinese cultural performances.
The One-Bedroom Beachfront Villa has Balinese decor, a dining area, a living area, a library and an outdoor patio with ocean views.

considerations.text: The hotel no longer provides bottled water or disposable in-room amenities; guests are advised to bring their own essentials and a drinking vessel to refill.
The Grand Club Pool is reserved for club guests.
WhataHotel notes the large resort may feel less intimate.
